A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MATE-3D benchmark and HyperScore evaluator. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original human ratings for 1,280 generated meshes, evaluator performance, ablations, and generalization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds evaluator comparisons, experimental controls, robustness tests, and predictions for Objaverse meshes.

M1.justification: The CLIP encoders, learnable condition prompts, conditional feature fusion, hypernetwork-generated mapping heads, and training losses are unchanged. Normal-map inputs are tested as alternatives; the proposed evaluator still uses texture renderings.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds evaluation of 2,000 Objaverse meshes, extending coverage beyond generated MATE-3D assets through a limited prediction-based check. MATE-3D's prompts, generators, and rating dimensions remain unchanged. The new GPTEval3D and T3Bench evaluator comparisons use MATE-3D.

E2.justification: Table 2 and the corresponding appendix comparisons add DreamReward, Q-Align, and DINO v2 + FT. New Table S5 evaluates GPTEval3D and T3Bench's quality and alignment evaluators, while Table 3 adds separately trained dimension-specific networks. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include separately trained networks, texture-only versus normal-only versus combined inputs, and azimuth rotations of 30, 45, and 60 degrees. The existing prompt-disjoint five-fold split, correlation metrics, and leave-one-category/method-out protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive tests of input representation, rotation robustness, and separate versus shared training, plus the Objaverse check. Its XGrad-CAM analysis gains a MultiScore comparison using the retained castle case. The former skeleton visualization and two main-text numerical case studies are removed; other existing analyses remain.

E5.justification: Five-fold averaging and subjective-rating outlier processing are unchanged. Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests for evaluator performance; the additions do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing matched result values are retained, but substantial comparison, ablation, robustness, and Objaverse results are added. Table 3 newly reports overall SRCC 0.778 for separately trained networks versus HyperScore's retained 0.792. New comparators also change some rankings: in v2 Table S15, DINO v2 + FT scores 0.663 for texture on held-out 3DTopia, exceeding HyperScore's unchanged 0.613.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(10), including the conditional fusion, hypernetwork mapping, regression loss, and disentangling loss, retain the same mathematics. No substantive formal definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same benchmark scope, four-dimensional evaluation objective, HyperScore proposal, and claim of superior aggregate performance on MATE-3D. The shortened conclusion preserves these claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the weak normal-map results to natural-image pretraining, argues that normalization provides scale invariance, and connects rotation robustness to varied training poses. It also expands the discussion of absolute versus pairwise scoring and separately trained versus shared evaluators.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 newly states that meshes are scaled into the unit ball before rendering. Conversely, v2 removes v1's explicit instruction to apply logistic score mapping before PLCC calculation; this does not establish that calibration actually stopped. Existing architecture details, optimization settings, hardware, and project-access statements remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including DINOv2, Q-Align, DreamReward, and additional generation methods, and removes the VQEG reference. Section 2.2 explicitly positions HyperScore as building on MPS, which was already cited in v1, while Appendix B.5 elaborates its relationship to GPTEval3D and T3Bench.

P1.justification: The section hierarchy and most prose are retained. Local revisions expand related work and the shared-evaluator motivation, replace the main qualitative discussion, shorten the conclusion, add acknowledgments, and redistribute some appendix discussion.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially expanded and revised. Figure 8 becomes a MultiScore/HyperScore XGrad-CAM comparison using a case from v1 Figure S6; v2 Figure S6 instead shows Objaverse examples. Tables 2, 3, and the generalization tables gain rows, and Tables S5, S12, and S13 are added. Core diagrams and the basic page layout remain.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the direct GPTEval3D/T3Bench comparisons, stronger DINOv2 baseline, and separate-training, input-type, and rotation controls improve scrutiny of the retained evaluator claims. These gains are tempered by the prediction-only Objaverse check, removal of PLCC calibration documentation, and incomplete highlighting of some new DINOv2 wins in the appendix tables. Overall, the empirical evidence becomes more informative, with a limited net quality gain.
